turns.text: bro quick one. do u need a dealer license in california to sell more than a few cars a year. its for dante's civics, i just wanna know the risk before i get into anything

In California you generally need a dealer license if you're "engaged in the business" of buying and selling vehicles. As a rough rule, selling more than about 5 vehicles in a 12-month period can trigger it, especially if you buy them to resell for profit. Selling your own personal vehicles occasionally is usually fine. Other things the DMV looks at: whether you buy at auction to flip, whether you hold titles without registering them in your name, and whether you advertise regularly. Selling without a license when you needed one can mean fines. Want the short checklist of what to stay under?
yeah short version. also im comparing used scan tool listings for weeks now and i wont go over 700, so i wanna check the rules first before i spend anything

Short version:
- Stay at or under about 5 sales a year (and check the DMV's current wording, since rules get updated)
- Title every car in your own name before you resell it
- Keep records of what you paid, fixed and sold for
- Don't make flipping your regular income stream without checking licensing
- Get everything in writing if you're working with a partner

For the DMV's exact rules, check the Occupational Licensing section of dmv.ca.gov. A scan tool is just a tool purchase, no license needed for that.

Sure. For a title transfer on your 2009 Tacoma, the vehicle section usually asks for:
- VIN (17 characters, on the dash by the windshield or the driver door jamb sticker)
- Year, make, model: 2009 Toyota Tacoma
- Current odometer reading
- License plate number
- Current owner/seller info and the new owner's info
